# Phase 16 (F3) — YouTube upload announcements

> Keyed against the Phase 16 branch tip (`worktree-agent-a625d41c3dd848a49`, the
> docs commit that carries this section). ⚠️ **Nothing below has met live
> Discord or a live YouTube API key.** The feed facts, on the other hand, ARE
> measured: every "measured 2026-09-02" note in this section came from real
> requests to `youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml` that day, and the feed those
> requests returned is kept verbatim as `tests/fixtures/youtube_feed.xml`.

## What section J actually measured, and what it changed

The design told the builder to measure the feed before writing the cog. Four
findings, three of which moved the design:

| Question | What the design assumed | What was measured |
|---|---|---|
| The entry fields | `yt:videoId`, `published`, `title`, `link href`, `yt:channelId`, `author/name` | **All present**, 15 entries per feed. Design confirmed. |
| ETag / `If-None-Match` → 304 | honoured, so an unchanged feed costs a 304 (D9) | ⚠️ **No `ETag` and no `Last-Modified` are sent at all.** There is no conditional GET to make. |
| Telling a Short apart | needs `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` and `contentDetails.duration` | ✅ **The feed does it for free**: a Short's `link href` is `youtube.com/shorts/<id>`, a video's is `watch?v=<id>`. D5 works keyless. |
| Availability | not considered | ⚠️ **~50%.** 30 requests, 2 s apart, one channel: **15 × 200, 12 × 404, 3 × 500**. |

The 404s are not the channel being wrong. Three other well-known channels took
1, 11 and 24 tries before their first 200, and throughout the whole run
`youtube.com/robots.txt`, the channel page itself and an unrelated Atom feed
answered 200 — while the failures carried YouTube's own
`Server: YouTube RSS Feeds server` header. It is their server, not the network,
and it is intermittent rather than per-channel. This became **KI-12**, and it is
the single fact that shaped the client most: **a 404 must never be read as "that
channel is gone".**

## `black_bloc/youtube.py` — the client and the parsing

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:19` | ⚠️ **`FEED_ATTEMPTS = 4` is a measurement, not a guess.** At the measured ~50% success rate, four independent tries miss about 1 sweep in 16; at three it is 1 in 8. Four also stays well inside one poll interval, so a retrying sweep never overlaps the next one. If the rate ever drops below ~25% this number stops being enough — that threshold is written into KI-12 as what would change the design. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:22` | A browser-ish `User-Agent` is sent because a default library UA is the classic WAF trip (the estate has been bitten before). ⚠️ Honest note: it was measured NOT to matter here — a bare `python-urllib` UA and a Chrome UA got the same 404/200 mix — so this is belt and braces, not a fix. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:37` | ⚠️ **The canonical link is the ONLY reliable way to turn a handle into a channel id**, and the design's suggested `"channelId":"UC…"` scrape is actively wrong. Measured 2026-09-02: on `youtube.com/@Kurzgesagt` that pattern matched **four ids, none of them the channel's own**; on `@GoogleDevelopers` it matched **nothing at all**. `<link rel="canonical">` was correct on both. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:44` | The refusal names the exact thing to paste (`youtube.com/channel/UC…`) AND the way a Lead can make handles work. A refusal that says only "I could not resolve that" leaves somebody with no next move. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:49` | ⚠️ **The wording deliberately blames the feed, not the member.** After four failures the likeliest explanation by far is KI-12, so the sentence says "usually the feed being flaky rather than the channel being wrong" and tells them to try again. Telling somebody their channel is wrong when it is not is the failure mode this sentence exists to prevent. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:80` | **`kind_of` reads the URL path, and that is the whole Shorts implementation.** Measured 2026-09-02 across two real feeds: every Short linked as `/shorts/<id>`, every full video as `watch?v=<id>` (Kurzgesagt 13/2, MrBeast 9/6). This is what lets D5 ship without an API key, which the design did not expect. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:91` | ⚠️ **The channel id comes from the ENTRY, never from the feed element.** Measured: the feed-level `<yt:channelId>` reads `sXVk37bltHxD1rDPwtNM8Q` — the `UC` prefix is **missing** — while every entry's carries the full `UCsXVk37bltHxD1rDPwtNM8Q`. Storing the feed-level one would write an id that can never be fetched again. `tests/test_youtube.py:66` pins it, fixture and all. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:91` | An entry with no `yt:videoId` is dropped rather than stored with a blank primary key; an entry with no `link` falls back to the `watch?v=` address, which then reads as a full video rather than a Short. Both are tolerance for a field the feed is not contractually obliged to send. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:108` | Unreadable XML raises `YouTubeError` with the parser's own message, while an EMPTY body is simply no videos. The difference matters: empty is what a 304 or a truncated response looks like and must not wake the degraded line; malformed is a real fault worth a sentence. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:142` | `classify_row` puts **live before short** because a broadcast can be under a minute and would otherwise be filed as a Short and silently skipped — the same silence, but for the wrong reason and with a misleading log line. A row whose length cannot be read is `unknown`, never guessed (checklist 10). |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:175` | `render` mirrors `golive.py:render` exactly, including the broken-template fallback (checklist 17) and `ping_prefix` for the mentions, and it IMPORTS both from `golive.py` rather than copying them (checklist 15). An empty title reads "a new video" so the default template can never post `****`. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:235` | ⚠️ **`fetch_feed` still takes and returns an ETag even though YouTube sends none.** Measured: no `ETag`, no `Last-Modified`, only `Cache-Control: public, max-age=900`. The parameter is kept because the column, the store helper and the 304 branch are all cheap and already correct — if YouTube ever adds the header the feature starts saving bandwidth with no code change. Today `etag` is always `NULL` and the 304 branch is exercised only by `tests/test_youtube.py`. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:235` | The retry loop returns on 200 **or** 304 and otherwise keeps trying; it does not distinguish 404 from 500, because measurement says both mean the same thing here — try again. The status codes seen are logged as a list on the final failure, so a genuinely dead channel is diagnosable from one log line. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:273` | `resolve` answers a bare id or a `/channel/` address **without any network call at all** — checked by `tests/test_youtube.py`, which asserts no request was made. That is the path `/uploads link-for` and the dashboard take most often, and it costs nothing and cannot flake. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:286` | With a key, `forHandle` is tried, then `forUsername`, and **then it still falls back to the page scrape**. Google's own API does not resolve every legacy `/c/` name, so the keyless path is not dead code once a key exists — it is the last rung of the same ladder. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:310` | ⚠️ **A title that cannot be fetched is blank, and the link still succeeds.** The channel id is the thing that matters; the title is decoration. Refusing a link because the flaky feed would not hand over a display name would make KI-12 into a user-facing failure for no gain. |
| `black_bloc/youtube.py:322` | Without a key `classify` returns `{}` — it never claims a kind it did not check (checklist 10). The caller then keeps whatever the URL path said, which is right for Shorts and admits ignorance about live streams. |

## `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py` — the sweep

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:141` | ⚠️ **`record_video` returns whether the row was NEW, and that boolean is the duplicate guard.** `INSERT OR IGNORE` on a `video_id` primary key means two overlapping sweeps cannot both announce: the second gets `rowcount == 0` and stops. This is the read-decide-write race of checklist 6 solved with the uniqueness constraint rather than a lock, because the key is already unique and global. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:160` | ⚠️ **The mode travels WITH the timestamp** (checklist 3 / "a status flag travels atomically with its value"). `announced_at`, `announced_message_id` and `mode` are set in one statement, so a later `/uploads mode on` cannot make a shadow-era row look like a real post. The dashboard's `state` column reads that stored mode, never the current one. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:253` | Checklist 28: discord.py re-raises a non-HTTP exception out of a loop and the loop then stays stopped for the life of the process. The handler records the error where `/uploads list` and the Health tab can see it, and restarts. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:260` | ⚠️ **The poll gap is re-read every tick, not frozen at boot.** `youtube_poll_minutes` is a settings key, so a change from the dashboard has to take effect without a redeploy; `change_interval` is only called when the number actually differs, because calling it every tick would reset the timer and the sweep would never fire. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:266` | The gap is read from the first guild the bot is in. Black Bloc is a single-server bot; this is the one place that assumption is written down rather than being implicit, and the fallback of 10 matches the registry default so the two can never silently disagree. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:272` | ⚠️ **A sweep counts as failed only when EVERY channel failed.** With KI-12's ~50% rate, one channel out of five failing is the normal state of the world, and letting that trip the degraded line would make the line meaningless within an hour. One log line per outage, at the point the sweep genuinely stops being trustworthy (mirrors `golive.py:_poll_failed`). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:295` | Two members who link the same channel: the first is polled, the second is warned about in the log and skipped — the same shape as the Twitch poller's double-link warning. The `/youtube link` command refuses this outright (checklist 16); `_pollable` is the belt for a row that got in some other way. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:311` | The ETag is written back on every 200 so a future YouTube that does send one starts working immediately; on the SEED path `mark_seeded` writes it instead, in the same statement that sets `seeded = 1`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:332` | ⚠️ **D10 lives here: linking counts everything already published as history.** Every current entry is stored with `announced_at` NULL and `mode` NULL, and `seeded` flips to 1. Without this the first sweep after a link would announce fifteen old videos at once, which is the single most obvious way this feature could embarrass somebody. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:352` | A classification failure is not a sweep failure: the URL-derived kind stands and the video is still announced. Losing the ability to spot a live stream is KI-11's known gap, not a reason to go silent. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:364` | ⚠️ **The row is written BEFORE the post, deliberately.** A crash between the two loses ONE announcement; the other order would repeat one on every restart. The design says it and `tests/cogs/content/test_youtube.py:324` proves it by exploding the channel's `send` and asserting the row exists with `announced_at` still NULL. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:364` | A member the bot cannot see anywhere still gets the video RECORDED. Storing it means they are not announced retroactively the moment they rejoin — the alternative is a burst of old uploads the day somebody comes back. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:393` | ⚠️ **D6's fallback, and the one place KI-11 lives in code.** With a key, whatever `videos.list` said is final. Without one, the only live signal available is the member's own go-live session — and it must be a session on platform `youtube` specifically, or a member streaming on Twitch would have their YouTube uploads silently swallowed. `tests/cogs/content/test_youtube.py:483` pins both halves. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:414` | ⚠️ **`off` returns before anything is rendered or logged.** Not even a `would_` line: `off` means the feature is not running, and a log full of would-lines from a feature nobody turned on is noise that hides the real ones. `shadow` is the mode that writes them. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:414` | Checklist 2: a test-mode refusal is `youtube.would_announce` with `reason=test_mode`, and a genuine failure is `youtube.post_failed`. They must be distinguishable at a glance, because "read the log" is the owner's verification method. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:477` | **The ONE guarded path.** Every upload post goes through here, and the `bot.guard` check happens before the channel is even fetched. Nothing else in this cog calls `channel.send`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:500` | Checklist 11: `allowed_mentions` is the enforcement and the `<@&…>` text is only the display. A YouTube video TITLE is attacker-controlled text going straight into a Discord message, so `everyone=False` here is what stops a video called `@everyone free nitro` from pinging the server. `tests/cogs/content/test_youtube.py` asserts it with a display name of `@everyone` too. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:512` | ⚠️ **D3 in one line: blank `youtube_channel_id` means the go-live channel.** The owner sets ONE place up and both feeds use it; pointing uploads elsewhere is opting out, not opting in. It also means the feature inherits whatever the owner already proved works for go-live. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:522` | A member asking `/youtube status` must never see a bare "no". The three reasons uploads are not being posted — the mode, no channel, or it is genuinely on — read as three different sentences, and the mode one names the mode so they can quote it to a Lead. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:597` | ⚠️ **`link_and_seed` is public because the WEB calls it too.** `/youtube link`, `/uploads link-for` and `POST /api/youtube/links` all land here, so the seed can never be done one way in Discord and another way on the site (checklist 15). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:597` | ⚠️ **A link SUCCEEDS even when the feed will not answer** — it returns 0 seeded and the poller seeds later. Refusing the link would hand KI-12 straight to the member as "your channel does not work". The reply and the API message both say the count, and the dashboard shows a "not yet" badge, so nobody is told a check happened that did not (checklist 10). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:640` | `/youtube status` defers to `_where_words` rather than printing the mode raw, and says what happens to Shorts, because those are the two things a streamer actually wants to know and both are settings they cannot see. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/youtube.py:850` | `_handle_of` stores the handle ONLY when the input was a handle — a `UC…` id is not a handle, and writing one into that column would make the dashboard show a fake `@name`. |

## `black_bloc/api/tools/youtube.py` and the Go-live page

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/api/tools/youtube.py:85` | ⚠️ **`state_of` reads the mode STORED on the row.** A row announced during a shadow week still reads `would` after the owner flips to `on`, which is the honest answer to "what happened to this video". Deriving it from the current mode would silently rewrite history every flip. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/youtube.py:101` | The GET carries `seeded` and `last_video` per row so the page can say "the feed has not answered for this one yet" — the API's job is to make KI-12 visible rather than to smooth it over. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/youtube.py:109` | The POST does its own resolve and its own owner check so it can raise its own worded 400/409, then calls the COG for the store-and-seed. One implementation of the rule, two sets of words for two audiences. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/youtube.py:162` | `unchanged_ratio` is `null`, not `0`, before any fetch has happened — the same honesty rule as `open_counts` and `followers`. "Nothing was unchanged" and "nothing has been counted" are different facts and must never render as the same number. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/youtube.py:162` | The status route answers even with the cog unloaded (`api_key_set: false`, `running: false`) rather than 503ing, because a Health-style panel that vanishes when the thing it monitors is down is the opposite of useful. The WRITE route does refuse in that state, through `require_cog`. |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:317` | The three states get three tones — announced `ok`, would `warn`, skipped `quiet` — so the table answers "did this actually go out?" at a glance without reading the Mode column. |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:320` | The sweep card is FIRST in the section, above the tables. With KI-12 in play, "is the sweep even working" is the question that decides how to read everything below it; the missing-API-key sentence sits here too, worded as a fact rather than a warning because unset is the intended state. |
| `site/public/assets/page-golive.js:370` | ⚠️ **The section is on the Go-live page, not a page of its own** — the same ownership answer as F14's Pings section. Uploads share the go-live channel by default, share the fan roles, and are about the same people; a second page would split one question across two surfaces. |

## Where else Phase 16 touched

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:138` | Schema **22**, additive only. `youtube_videos.video_id` is the primary key rather than an autoincrement id — the duplicate guard in `record_video` depends on it, and a YouTube video id is already globally unique. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:42` | The default template lives beside `GOLIVE_TEMPLATE` so `youtube.py` can import it rather than declaring a second copy (checklist 15) — the same reason `golive.py` imports its own. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:44` | ⚠️ **The floor of 5 minutes has a measured reason, and the validator says it.** The feed answers `Cache-Control: public, max-age=900` — 15 minutes — so polling faster than the cache cannot find anything sooner. The refusal explains that rather than just naming a number. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:35` | ⚠️ **`/settings clear` moved from static choices to an autocomplete, and Phase 16 is why.** Two new channel/role keys took `CLEARABLE_KEYS` to **27**, past Discord's hard ceiling of 25 choices on a command option. The alternatives were dropping keys from the menu — which would break checklist 33, since a key you cannot clear from Discord is not configurable both ways — or doing what `/settings set-value` already did. `tests/cogs/test_core.py` asserts the list is now over 25, so the reason cannot be forgotten. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:287` | The autocomplete filters on a substring of the KEY, so typing `youtube` narrows to the namespace. The 25-item slice is Discord's response cap, not a design choice. |
| `tests/test_youtube.py:74` | This test is the record that Shorts detection is free. If YouTube ever stops using `/shorts/` links it fails here first, loudly, against the captured fixture — and the fix is then `YOUTUBE_API_KEY` plus `classify`, which is already written and already tested. |
| `tests/test_youtube.py:225` | ⚠️ **A test that asserts an ABSENCE.** It exists so that a future session reading `fetch_feed`'s etag plumbing does not "fix" the missing 304 handling — the measurement, not the code, is what says YouTube sends no validator. |
| `tests/test_youtube.py:244` | The retry test encodes the measured failure mix (404, 500, 404, 200) rather than a tidy one, and asserts the exact number of attempts, so shrinking `FEED_ATTEMPTS` fails visibly. |
| `tests/test_youtube.py:291` | The handle-resolution test deliberately puts a WRONG `"channelId":"UC…"` in the page body beside the right canonical link, so an implementation that goes back to scraping that field fails. That is exactly the bug the measurement found. |
| `tests/cogs/content/test_youtube.py:578` | The test that says a dead feed leaves the link alone. It is the guard against the most damaging plausible bug in this phase: reading KI-12's 404 as "this channel does not exist" and unlinking a real member. |

# Phase 17 — chat long-term memory, and the requests state machine

> Keyed against the Phase 17 branch `worktree-agent-a268aa7fa2979dd4a` (the docs
> commit carries this section). The phase ADDED `black_bloc/chat_memory.py`,
> `black_bloc/chat_distil.py`, `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py`,
> `black_bloc/api/tools/chat_memory.py` and their four mirrored test files, and touched
> `requests.py`, `cogs/community/requests.py`, `api/tools/requests.py`, `chat_llm.py`,
> `groq.py`, `settings_store.py`, `logkinds.py`, `personas.py`, `storage/db.py`
> (schema **23**), `api/status.py`, `api/server.py`, `bot.py`, `site/mock/*` and
> `site/public/assets/{page-requests,page-chat,labels}.js`. ⚠️ **No key above this
> section was re-keyed** — the phase appended to `settings_store.py`, `logkinds.py` and
> `storage/db.py` rather than editing them in place, but `requests.py`,
> `cogs/community/requests.py` and `api/tools/requests.py` WERE edited in place, so any
> older key into those three should be trusted by anchor text, not by number.

## `black_bloc/chat_memory.py` — the rules, the shapes and the storage

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:278` | ⚠️ **`normalise` and `has_phrase` are wrappers around `chat.py`'s, imported LATE inside the function on purpose.** `settings_store.py` imports this module for its choice tuples, and `chat.py → chat_data.py → settings_store.py` is a cycle at module level. `chat_data.py` already uses the same late-import trick; duplicating the two functions would have broken checklist 15 instead. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:71` | Only the DOUBLE-quote family and the backtick are banned. An apostrophe is not a quote mark in English, and banning it would drop "they're", "don't" and half the legitimate notes. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:90` | The availability list is the GABI rule made mechanical: the bot must never claim somebody is online, free, or anywhere. `lives in` and `based in` are here rather than under sensitive because location is an availability claim first. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:162` | ⚠️ **`OUTCOMES` is checked against THREADS as well as notes, and §J is why.** Run 1 of the measurement had the model return the thread `"namu quitting the server"`; `quit` was already on the list and did not match `quitting`, because `has_phrase` is word-boundary exact. The departure family (`quitting`, `quits`, `leaving`, `departure(s)`) plus `banned`/`kicked`/`muted`/`warned`/`timed out` were added for that one measured leak, and run 2 dropped all three attempts. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:185` | `straight` was REMOVED from the sensitive list after §J: it collided with "likes straight answers", which §D2-definition names as a KEEP example. A false positive costs one note; that one would have cost a whole class of legitimate ones. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:319` | ⚠️ **`other_names` is the only guard that can catch an arbitrary third-person name**, because a phrase list cannot enumerate the server's members. The cog passes it, so it is guild-aware; a note naming any other member is dropped. It is not a proof — see `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:332` | `why_dropped` returns the rule's NAME rather than a bool so the log and the tests can say which rule fired, and so `Distilled.dropped` can carry rule names and never the text. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:389` | ⚠️ **`Profile.visible` is the D4 guard at the DATA level, not the prompt level.** GABI relies on telling the model not to use DM notes in public; here a `where = dm` note is filtered out of both the reply block AND the prompt the next distillation sees, so it cannot be re-emitted into the server scope by a model that ignores an instruction. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:254` | The distil prompt states the KEEP list and the THROW AWAY list in the model's own terms, and `parse_distilled` re-checks every one of them. The prompt is the cheap filter; the parser is the one that is load-bearing. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:488` | A code fence is the one wrapper tolerated. §J saw none in 29 calls with JSON mode on, but the cost of tolerating one is three lines and the cost of not is a whole conversation's distillation. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:504` | ⚠️ **Structural problems are a no-op; one bad ITEM is a dropped item.** Bad JSON, an unknown key, a non-string note or an over-long `call_me` all return `None` and write nothing — never a partial profile. A note that breaks a privacy rule is dropped on its own and the rest of the profile still saves, which is what §D2-definition rule 2 asks for. An over-long NOTE is treated as a dropped item rather than a whole-profile reject; the design's "over-length fields → None" is read as the top-level fields. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:546` | `widest` is why a note learned in a DM and then again in the server ends up `server`: dedupe would otherwise let the newer (DM) copy NARROW an existing public note, silently losing it from public replies. Widening is the safe direction and loses nothing. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:578` | `merge` caps AFTER merging, so a newly learned preference always survives and the oldest drops off. The caps are `chat_memory_notes_max` / `_threads_max`, not constants. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:619` | `drop_matching` matches on NORMALISED substrings, because `/memory forget-this` asks a person to type a few of the words they just read, not to quote a line exactly. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:715` | ⚠️ **One table, one meaning: a row in `chat_memory_optout` means "this person is NOT on the server's default".** Under `optout` consent a row means do-not-remember; under `optin` it means remember-me. That is what lets D1 be a settings key rather than a schema change — the alternatives were a second table or a `choice` column the design's schema does not have. `set_remembered` is the only writer, so no caller has to think about which way round it is. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:722` | `overridden` returns `None` on a read failure and `remembered(None)` is `False`, so an unreadable table means nobody is remembered. Failing towards forgetting is the only safe direction for a privacy feature. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:702` | `forget_everywhere` is keyed on the member alone, not on the guild: `on_member_remove` fires for one guild, and D3 says leaving clears the profile at once. A single-guild bot makes the difference academic today, and the wider delete is the one that stays right if that changes. |
| `black_bloc/chat_memory.py:777` | `expire(days=0)` returns 0 rather than deleting everything — `chat_memory_retention_days = 0` means FOREVER, and the read that makes that true has to be here rather than at the caller. |

## `black_bloc/chat_distil.py` — the run

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:69` | ⚠️ **`expiring` SELECTs the rows the sweep is about to delete, before `sweep_window` runs.** The whole design of the feature is that distillation is on the sweep and never on the reply path; `tests/cogs/content/test_chat.py` asserts the ORDER, because getting it backwards would silently distil nothing. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:98` | Two member turns minimum, and not one `about_staff` word. The staff gate is checked on the MEMBER turns only — the bot's own reply mentioning "modmail" must not disqualify an ordinary conversation, and §J confirmed `about_staff` catches the appeal window on the member's side. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:106` | The Groq client is built in its own slot (`MEMORY_TIER`) rather than sharing `SIMPLE`. With `chat_memory_model` set to something other than `chat_simple_model`, one shared slot would rebuild — and leak — an `aiohttp` session on every alternating call. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:106` | The ledger row is written for the ERROR case too, with `client.model` rather than the (possibly blank) setting, so a month of failed distillations is visible on the Spend section rather than invisible. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:195` | A capped or fused month BREAKS the loop rather than continuing: the allowance is a global fact, so re-checking it per conversation would spend the rest of the sweep proving the same thing. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:195` | A DM has no guild, so it files under `dev_guild_id` with `where = dm`. One profile per person, two scopes inside it — D4. |
| `black_bloc/chat_distil.py:240` | Expiry runs on the same sweep rather than a loop of its own, for the same reason the window sweep does: a bot that restarts weekly would otherwise never reach a timer that only fires monthly. |

## `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py` — `/memory`

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py:103` | ⚠️ **The group is top-level `/memory`, NOT `/chat memory` as the design says.** Discord applies `default_permissions` to the whole top-level command, and `/chat` is `STAFF_ONLY` — a member-visible subcommand under it is impossible without opening the whole `/chat` group to members, which would break the house rule about not rendering a control somebody cannot use. Listed in the design's Deviations. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:16` | ⚠️ **`/memory` is HIDDEN while `chat_memory_mode` is off**, the same way `/rolemenu` and `/request` follow their own modes. The feature ships off, so at deploy the command is not in the tree at all — a member never meets a command whose only answer is "that is turned off". `MEMORY_IS_OFF` still exists for the window between a mode flip and the next command sync. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py:107` | A DM has no guild, so `home` falls back to `dev_guild_id` — the same single-guild assumption `chat_distil` makes. With neither, the command says so in words rather than doing nothing. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py:119` | `ready` is the one gate: no server, no database, or the feature off. Each is a different sentence, because "nothing happened" for three different reasons is three different things to do about it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py:88` | ⚠️ **`profile_words` is the enforcement mechanism for §D2-definition rule 7.** If a line would embarrass the bot when read back to the person it is about, it is content and should never have been kept. Everything the bot holds is printable here, in plain words, including the DM mark. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py:205` | `off` opts out AND wipes, in that order, so a crash between them leaves the person opted out with a stale profile rather than opted in with none — the safe half. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/chat_memory.py:234` | `on_member_remove` forgets before checking anything else: D3 says leaving the server clears the profile at once, whatever `chat_memory_retention_days` says. |

## `black_bloc/api/tools/chat_memory.py` and the Chat page's Memory section

| Key | Note |
|---|---|

# Phase 18 (F19) — raid trains

> Keyed against the Phase 18 branch tip (`worktree-agent-a1c38e3df0f71fa7e`, the
> docs commit that carries this section). ⚠️ **Nothing below has met live
> Discord.** No lineup has been posted, no reminder DM has ever arrived, and no
> member has claimed an hour. Everything here is test-suite evidence.

## What section J actually measured, and what it changed

The design told the builder to read `events.py`'s scheduled-event helper FIRST
and only ship `raidtrain_scheduled_event` on if it was reusable **without
editing `events.py`** (which is read-only in a parallel build).

**Finding: it is importable, and it is still not reusable.**
`cogs/community/events.py:570 create_scheduled_event(bot, guild, row)` is a
module-level function, so `from ..community.events import create_scheduled_event`
would compile. It is disqualified by what it does, not by where it lives:

1. It ends with `set_scheduled(bot.db, row["id"], made.id)`, which runs
   `UPDATE events SET scheduled_event_id = ? WHERE id = ?`. Passing it a raid
   train would stamp a Discord event id onto **whatever `events` row happens to
   share that id** — silent cross-table corruption, and exactly the class of bug
   this file exists to stop somebody re-introducing.
2. It gates on the `events_create_scheduled` setting, so raid trains would
   inherit the events feature's switch and D13's own key would be dead.
3. Every line it logs is `event.*`, so a raid train's calendar entry would never
   appear under `/raidtrains logs` or the Raid trains section's log filter.

**So D13 ships `raidtrain_scheduled_event = false`**, per §J's instruction, and
the key is NOT a dead switch: `_maybe_scheduled_event` is twenty lines of this
cog's own that call `guild.create_scheduled_event` directly, with raid-train log
kinds and no writes outside `raid_trains`. `find_scheduled_event` — the one
genuinely reusable piece, a pure cache-then-fetch lookup with no table in it —
IS imported from `events.py` for the cancel path (checklist 15).

⚠️ A second reason the default would be academic today: `create_scheduled_event`
refuses outright while `bot.guard` exists, and so does ours. Under TEST_MODE no
scheduled event can be made at all, whichever way the key is set.

## `black_bloc/raidtrain.py` — the pure half

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:18` | ⚠️ **`SLOT_COUNT_MAX = 24` is a Discord limit, not a taste.** A slot line renders at roughly 85 characters (`#12 <t:…:t>–<t:…:t> — <@700000000000000002> (https://twitch.tv/somelogin)`), and a message is capped at 2000, so 24 lines plus the header is the last size that certainly fits in ONE message. It has to be one message because the lineup is edited in place rather than reposted. r3dlabs runs 50-slot trains; ours refuses in words and says why. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:20` | `REMINDER_LATE_MINUTES` is checklist 31: a due-row sweep must age rows out. A slot whose start is more than this far past does not get a late DM telling somebody to go live for an hour that has gone — `missed_reminders` stamps it instead, so it also stops being carried by every future sweep. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:31` | The transition table is the ONE place a status move is decided; `may_move` and `allowed_moves` are both derived from it, and `allowed_moves` exists so a refusal can say what IS possible in words rather than printing a status list at somebody. `cancelled` is reachable only from `open`/`locked` — the design's rule, so a train that has already started is finished rather than un-run. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:83` | `_value` reads a sqlite `Row`, a plain dict or an object with attributes. That is what keeps every helper in this file testable with dict fixtures while the cog hands it real rows — the same trick `render_lineup` needs to be a pure function. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:95` | ⚠️ **Times belong to the POSITION, never to the person.** Slots are created eagerly at `create` with their times already in them, so `swap` moves five holder columns and touches no timestamp. A design that stored times on the claim would have to rewrite them on every reorder, and a half-finished reorder would leave a lineup with two 8pm slots. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:106` | `ends_at` prefers the SLOT rows' own `ends_at` over `starts_at + minutes × count`. The arithmetic is the fallback for a train whose rows are unreadable; the rows are the truth, because they are what a swap and a future per-slot length would move. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:147` | `caps_ok` treats **0 as no ceiling**, which is why the settings validator lets the key go to 0 and its max-reason sentence says so. An organizer's `assign` never calls this — D10 says the cap is for self-service claims only. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:189` | A holder is written `<@id>`, and every send/edit of this text goes out under `AllowedMentions(users=False)` (see the cog's `_mentions`). The mention RENDERS as their name and pings nobody — which matters because the lineup is edited on every claim and a pinging edit would notify twenty people twenty times. Checklist 11. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:210` | ⚠️ **`render_lineup` is the whole post, and it is re-rendered from the rows every time rather than patched.** One function means the Discord post, `/raidtrain status` and the dashboard's `lineup` field can never disagree about what the lineup says. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:252` | The reminder names BOTH neighbours with their twitch.tv links, because the thing a slot holder actually needs at T-30 is not "your slot is soon" — it is who to watch for the incoming raid and who to send the audience to. That is the request's own wording ("who they will be raided by and the person they raid next"). |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:278` | ⚠️ **`due_reminders` deliberately excludes a slot whose start has already gone by** (`start <= floor`), and `missed_reminders` picks exactly those up. They are two functions rather than one flag because the two outcomes are different actions — send, versus stamp and stay quiet — and the cog must be able to do the second without the first. |
| `black_bloc/raidtrain.py:314` | `due_checkins` takes the live user ids as an ARGUMENT rather than reaching for `golive.open_sessions` itself. That keeps this module Discord-free and database-free, and it is what makes the check-in window testable without a session table. |

## `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py` — the cog

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:146` | `create_train` writes the train AND every slot in one commit. Slots-on-create is what makes `position` meaningful from the first second: `/raidtrain list` can say which hours are free before anybody has claimed anything, which is half of what the request asked for ("slot availability"). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:228` | ⚠️ **`take_slot`'s `WHERE id = ? AND user_id IS NULL` is the race guard, and `rowcount` is how the caller learns it lost.** Checklist 6 wants a lock AND a database constraint; the lock is `_lock(train_id)`, and this conditional UPDATE is the constraint — a partial unique index could not be used here because the per-member ceiling is a SETTING (0 = unlimited), and a schema cannot encode a value the owner may change. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:250` | `swap_holders` moves five columns and no time (see `raidtrain.py:95`). `reminded_at` travels WITH the person, so somebody already reminded for 8pm who is moved to 9pm is not reminded again — the alternative, clearing it, would DM them twice about one train. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:290` | `stamp_slot` interpolates a column name into SQL, so it validates against a three-item allowlist first and raises otherwise. The allowlist form is deliberate (default-deny, per the estate's export rule); an exclusion list would leak the moment a column was added. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:335` | The DM helper is this cog's own rather than an import from `cogs/community/requests.py`, which was being rewritten in parallel by Phase 17. It is six lines and it catches everything, because a member with DMs closed is a normal state, not an error — the CALLER turns that into a `raidtrain.dm_failed` line so silence is never silent. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:409` | One `asyncio.Lock` per train. The contended path is two members claiming the same open slot in the same second, and the second half of that guard is the conditional UPDATE above. The sweep takes the same lock, so a claim cannot land between "read the slots" and "promote the train to live". |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:436` | Checklist 28: discord.py re-raises a non-HTTP exception out of a `tasks.loop` and the loop then stays dead for the life of the process. `@sweep.error` restarts it and records the failure where `/api/raidtrains/status` and the Health tab can see it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:442` | `_retime` re-reads `raidtrain_poll_minutes` every tick instead of freezing the boot value, so changing the gap on the dashboard takes effect without a restart. Same shape as the YouTube poller. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:477` | ⚠️ **Checklist 32: `guild.unavailable` is skipped.** An outage that hides a guild must not be read as "this train has no slots" — nothing is promoted, nothing is finished, nothing is stamped for a guild Discord is not currently telling us about. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:493` | The clock does all three moves and the poller owns all of them: auto-lock at the start (D11 — fixed, deliberately not a key: a train that keeps taking sign-ups while it runs cannot have a raid order), `→ live`, then `→ done` once the last slot's own `ends_at` has passed. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:521` | ⚠️ **`reminded_at` is stamped BEFORE the DM is attempted, and that order is the whole point.** A crash between the two loses ONE reminder; the other order would re-send on every sweep for as long as the failure lasted. The same rule as `youtube.record_video` returning False for a duplicate. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:538` | Checklist 2: `raidtrain.remind` (sent), `raidtrain.would_remind` (shadow) and `raidtrain.dm_failed` (tried and refused) are three different kinds, because the owner's verification method is reading the log and those three must be distinguishable at a glance. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:572` | Check-in reads `golive.open_sessions` — the one signal, not a second detector. It is also why **KI-16** exists: a holder whose presence is hidden and who is not Twitch-linked is never seen. Accepted, same limit as F1. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:617` | D7: blank `raidtrain_channel_id` borrows `events_announce_channel_id`, so a server sets up ONE place rather than two. Same pattern as `youtube_channel_id` borrowing `golive_channel_id`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:627` | ⚠️ **The only role that may be mentioned is the configured ping role.** `users=False` is what makes the in-place edits safe (see `raidtrain.py:189`), and `everyone=False` is what stops a train titled `@everyone` from doing anything. Checklist 11. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:643` | The one guarded path to a channel. A channel TEST_MODE refuses is logged as `raidtrain.post_skipped_test_mode` and returns None — never raised, so a refused post can never abort the state change that preceded it (checklist 12: the important thing first, cosmetics last). `no_channel_configured` and `channel_not_visible` are separate named reasons because the fixes differ. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:720` | The thread is opened on the message that was actually posted, and the guard is told it owns the thread (`own_channel`) so the "train moves" lines may be sent into it while test mode is on — the same allowance temp voice uses for the rooms it makes itself. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:746` | See §J above: this is the raid-train-owned scheduled-event creator. It refuses under TEST_MODE with `raidtrain.would_create_scheduled` (checklist 1: a side effect the HTTP guard cannot see checks `bot.guard` itself), and it never writes outside `raid_trains`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:817` | ⚠️ **The lineup is EDITED, never reposted.** One message is the whole public record of a train, so a member who bookmarked it keeps a live view; a repost would leave a trail of stale lineups and would ping the ping role again each time. A failed edit is a logged `raidtrain.post_failed`, not an exception — the claim that caused it has already been committed. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:858` | ⚠️ **Mode `off` refuses EVERY member command in words**, naming `/raidtrains mode` — not a hidden command and not a dead one. The staff group deliberately keeps working while off, because `mode` is how you turn it on. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:877` | D2: organizer = the configured role OR staff. It is not `default_permissions`, because Discord's permission lock cannot express "or this role"; the gate is at runtime and the refusal NAMES who may do it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:988` | ⚠️ **Every command that ends up editing the lineup DEFERS first, and every refusal that can be decided without touching Discord answers BEFORE the defer.** Checklist 8 and 24: `_refresh_lineup` fetches and edits a message, message edits are rate-limited, and discord.py sleeps through a 429 — so the 3-second interaction window would expire and the member would see "The application did not respond". `tests/cogs/content/test_raidtrain.py` asserts `response.deferred` on all seven, so removing a defer fails by name. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1007` | The order of the refusals is the order they cost: the train's status, then the per-member ceiling, then whether the slot exists, then the race. Each returns a sentence, and the last one is the only one that can be reached by two people at once. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1127` | `submit_train` reuses `events.py`'s `start_error` and `START_IN_THE_PAST` rather than writing a second pair of date sentences (checklist 15). The zone is the member's own `/timezone`, so nothing new about time was invented for this phase (D15). |
| `black_bloc/cogs/content/raidtrain.py:1190` | `_numbers` refuses out-of-range sizes BEFORE a row is written, and its sentence names Discord's one-message limit as the reason rather than just quoting a number. |

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/api/tools/raidtrain.py:103` | Every id leaves as a STRING. A Discord snowflake is bigger than a JavaScript safe integer, and a number that quietly loses its last digits on the page is the worst kind of bug — it looks like it worked. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/raidtrain.py:145` | ⚠️ **`/status` is declared BEFORE `/{train_id}`.** FastAPI takes the first route that matches and `{train_id}` is typed `int`, so the other order would answer `/api/raidtrains/status` with a 422 about a path parameter — a bare status code in front of a person, which the estate rule forbids. The mock's matcher has the same first-match rule and the same declaration order. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/raidtrain.py:189` | The create route does its own worded 400s and then calls the COG for the lineup post, so one implementation of "post the lineup" serves both surfaces and each audience gets its own words. Same split as `/api/youtube/links`. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/raidtrain.py:254` | ⚠️ **One route fills and empties a seat**, keyed on `member_id` being null. Two routes would be two places to forget the Twitch-link check, and the page's slot grid has one control per row either way. |
| `site/public/assets/page-events.js:180` | A control nobody may use is NOT RENDERED: "Take off" only appears on a taken slot, "Put somebody in" only on an open one, and neither appears at all once `editable` is false. The estate rule prefers a missing control to one that refuses. |
| `site/public/assets/page-events.js:280` | ⚠️ **Raid trains are a SECTION on the Events page, not a page of their own** — the Events page already owns "what is scheduled", and a second surface answering the same question is the duplicate-surface bug the docs standard names. The mode warning sits at the top of the section, above the table, for the same reason the YouTube sweep card does: it decides how to read everything below it. |

So a second cog can add a role through it by importing it — `role_menus.py` never had to be edited, and the §J fallback (writing our own `_add_role`) was not needed. This is the measurement §J asked for. |

## The helpers

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/applications.py:1` | The module is shaped like `rolegrants.py`, not like a cog: constants, the wording every surface shares, the validators, and the async storage helpers. The cog and `api/tools/applications.py` are two sets of words over one implementation. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:1` | ⚠️ **`MODES` and `RETRY_DAYS_DEFAULT` are imported FROM `settings_store`, not declared here.** `golive.py` does the same with its template: the registry owns a decided default, and importing the other way round would be a cycle (`applications` → `golive` → `settings_store`). |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:answers_json` | The snapshot stores `{label, answer}` pairs, so editing a question later changes the modal and never the history. Recorded as an accepted residual in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:read_answers` | An unreadable snapshot logs a warning and renders as no answers rather than raising — a card that cannot be drawn is worse than a card with nothing on it, and the row is still decidable. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:add_question` | The new question takes the LOWEST free slot, not `count + 1`, so removing question 2 and adding another puts it back at 2 rather than leaving a hole or colliding with the `UNIQUE (form_id, position)` index. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:decide_application` | Asks `may_move` BEFORE the UPDATE, so a status that is not a transition raises rather than silently matching no rows — the two failures would otherwise be indistinguishable. The UPDATE itself still carries `AND status = 'pending'`, which is what makes two clicks safe. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:create_application` | ⚠️ **The `open_application` check is the polite answer; the partial unique index is the guard.** Two clicks a millisecond apart both pass the read, and the second INSERT raises `sqlite3.IntegrityError` — caught here and answered as "you already have one waiting" rather than reaching the member as a broken modal. Checklist item 6. `tests/test_applications.py::test_the_unique_index_catches_a_second_application_the_check_did_not_see` stubs the read out so the INSERT really is the thing that loses; it fails if the `except` is removed. |
| `black_bloc/applications.py:last_decision` | Deliberately looks only at `approved` and `denied`. A withdrawn application is the member changing their mind, and starting a 30-day cooling period on it would punish somebody for tidying up. |

## The cog

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:review_channel` | Four fallbacks in one place: the form's own channel, `applications_channel_id`, `rolemenu_approval_channel_id`, `staff_channel_id`. The card then goes through `role_menus.card_target`, which is what redirects it to the test channel while the guard is on. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:may_decide` | The approver ROLE wins, then staff. A refusal names the role and says which command points the form at a different one — never a bare "you can't do that". |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:_hand_over` | ⚠️ **Shadow logs `application.would_grant` and adds nothing** (review-checklist item 1: the HTTP guard cannot see a role edit, so the cog checks the mode itself). The design's log list named only `would_post` and `would_dm`; this is the third, and it is in `## Deviations`. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:_hand_over` | A member who ALREADY holds the role is recorded rather than re-added. Without this the approve path sends Discord a duplicate role in `member.edit` — found by `tests/api/tools/test_applications.py`, where the seeded member wears the form's role already. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:_approve` | The order is decide → role → grant → card → DM, and the row is re-read after `_hand_over` so `grant_id` is on the object the card and the API answer with. Checklist item 12: the irreversible thing first, cosmetics last; `edit_card` swallows its own errors. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:ApplyModal` | The modal is built at open time from `application_questions`, so the questions are data the owner edits, never code. Discord's five-box cap is enforced at `add_question`/`replace_questions`, which is why the modal can trust its input. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:open_form_modal` | Every refusal a member can meet is checked BEFORE the modal opens — off, no questions, closed, already waiting — so nobody types three paragraphs into a form that is going to refuse them. The cooling check is the one exception: it needs the answers-free path in `submit_application` too, because a form can be applied for from two entry points. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:nudge_mentions` | ⚠️ **The decided card pings EXACTLY one person: the `owner_user_id` the form names.** Checklist item 11 says allow only the configured mention, and D8's whole point is that somebody is told to go and click the twitch.tv invite — a card that renders `@owner` without notifying them would look like it did its job and quietly not have. With no owner set it is `AllowedMentions.none()`. |
| `black_bloc/command_visibility.py:16` | ⚠️ **`applications_mode: ("apply",)` — the MEMBER group is hidden while the feature is off, the staff group is not.** Otherwise `/apply` sits in the picker refusing everybody, which the process rule calls the worse half of "prefer not rendering a control someone cannot use". `/applications` stays, because a Lead has to be able to turn it back on from Discord. Side effect: `applications_mode` ships **off**, so every boot now spends KI-2's second guild sync — already an accepted cost there. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/applications.py:applications_approve` | `extras={"staff_only": True}` because the gate is two hops away (`_decide` → `may_decide` → `require_staff`) and `settings_store.is_staff_command` only walks one. The alternative was adding the path to `GATE_IS_TWO_HOPS_AWAY` in `tests/test_bot.py`, which hides the fact in a test instead of stating it on the command. |

## The API and the page

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/api/tools/applications.py:checked` | ⚠️ **It is `async` and it `await`s inside the `try`.** The first version wrapped the call only, which builds a coroutine and catches nothing — every `ApplicationError` escaped as a 500 until the tests caught it. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/applications.py:build_router` | `/status` and `/forms` are registered BEFORE `/{application_id}`, because FastAPI matches in declaration order and `status` is not an int. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/applications.py:applications_form_delete` | Deleting a form with somebody waiting answers **409 in words** with the count and the `open:false` alternative. A form is data the owner made; refusing is cheaper than orphaning three people's applications. |
| `site/public/assets/page-rolemenus.js:applicationsMode` | The page already owns a two-way `modeSwitch`; importing `ui.js`'s would be a duplicate declaration in the same module scope, so the three-way one is its own function built from the same `segment` + `saveSetting` pieces. |
| `site/public/assets/page-rolemenus.js:formEditor` | The question rows are read from the DOM, not from the array they were pushed into, so Up/Down really do decide the stored order. |
| `site/public/assets/page-rolemenus.js:applicationsSection` | ⚠️ **The section is on the Role menus page, not a page of its own** — the same ownership answer as F14's Pings and F3's uploads. "How does somebody get a role here" is one question and it has one surface. |
| `site/public/assets/page-rolemenus.js:applicationsSection` | The section's DOM id is **`sect-applications`** (`ui.js:section` adds the prefix), so the review link is `/rolemenus.html#sect-applications`. Rendered against the mock on 2026-09-02: the off/shadow/on switch, two pending cards with their answers, the decided table, both forms with their question counts, an Apply-button card each and the settings panel — no console errors, and the Edit button opens the editor with the form's three questions in it. |
| `site/mock/check.mjs:GUARDED` | The guarded entry carries `IDS.test_channel_id` rather than `'{test_channel_id}'`: `checkGuard` fills the PATH but not the BODY, so a placeholder in the body reaches the route as literal text and gets a 400 instead of the guard's 409. |

## One web write, one log row (owner report, 2026-09-03)

> Keyed against `df393ab` (the `fix/web-write-double-log` merge), then re-keyed by
> the requests third pass to `feat/requests-third-pass`. ⚠️ The original header
> line here said "commit **HEADSHA**" — a placeholder that was never filled in;
> `df393ab` is the merge and `19d2f7d` is the docs commit that carries this
> section. Owner: *"The app double posted all messages with a web.request and a
> request"*.

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:357` | ⚠️ **`kind_via` is `bare()` read backwards, and the ONLY place the `web.` head is put on.** Six modules used to build `f"{WEB}." if via == VIA_WEBSITE else ""` for themselves (pings, rolemenu_panels, applications twice, role_menus, tempvoice); six copies of an inverse is how one of them drifts from `bare()` and a kind stops classifying. `test_no_module_builds_the_web_head_for_itself` fails if a seventh appears. |
| `black_bloc/api/writes.py:185` | `note()` survives, but only for events **the route is the sole logger of** — `web.request.filed`, `web.request.updated`, the comments, the withdraw, the raid-train and role-menu CRUD. Where a shared bot function already logs, the route passes `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and notes nothing: that pairing was the 2026-09-03 double post, two rows and two embeds for one click. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:284` | `via` is **keyword-only with a Discord default** so the four slash callers keep writing bare `request.*` kinds untouched, and only the dashboard's `_decide` opts into the `web.` head. (Third pass: `mark_ready`, `accept` and `send_back` take the same keyword and pass it straight through.) The same shape is on `resume_request`, `events.apply_decision`, `events.cancel_event`, `polls.store_poll`/`apply_decision`/`close_poll`/`cancel_poll`, `role_menus.apply_request_decision`, `modmail.close_ticket`, `honeypot.ban_hit`/`make_trap_channel`, `tempvoice.make_creator_channel`/`forget_creator`, `automod.save_rule`/`apply_case`/`punish` and the six `modcmds` punishers. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:336` | `details["via"] = via` is written even though the kind already carries the head, because `via_of()` prefers what the writer recorded over what the kind says. Belt and braces: a row keeps saying "Website" even if somebody later renames the kind. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:302` | The route's whole job here is now `via=VIA_WEBSITE` — the deleted `note(f"web.request.{status}")` was the defect. `request_status` still notes `web.request.updated` beside it, because assignee/priority/notes are a **different** change from the status move and nothing else logs them. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modcmds.py:161` | `refuse_in_test_mode` takes `via` too, so a dashboard punish refused by TEST_MODE leaves `web.mod.would_ban` rather than a bare one that reads as a Discord action. It is the actor's row, not a bot-emitted consequence — the `mod.*_failed` and `request.dm_failed` family deliberately stay bare. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/automod.py:178` | `punish` heads every row it leaves, not just the successful one: delete/warn/timeout and their `would_`/`_failed` twins are all outcomes of one actor's click, so they belong to the same Via. This is why the dashboard's Apply-now now leaves `web.automod.*` and no `web.mod.apply` — the automod rows ARE the event, and `mod.apply` was a second framing of it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/moderation/modmail.py:616` | `send_reply` was a **false positive** in the survey that found these: it logs only `modmail.dm_failed`, nothing on success, so `web.modmail.reply` is the route's own and stays. `close_ticket` next to it did double, and does not. |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:272` | `_branches` unwraps `kind_via(...)` so the dynamic-kind table does not need forty new entries: a literal inside it yields BOTH the bare and the `web.` form. An f-string inside it still needs `KNOWN_DYNAMIC`, keyed on the INNER expression — which is why the pre-existing keys like `f'request.{wanted}'` kept working and just grew their `web.` twins. |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:459` | The mechanical guard for checklist 34. It resolves each route's imports to real module files, asks what kinds those functions log (following helpers within their own module, and reading `KNOWN_DYNAMIC` for the f-strings), and fails on any `note()` whose `bare()` kind is in that set. ⚠️ Helpers under `api/` are excluded (`API`) — `note` itself logs whatever it is handed, so without that filter every route matches itself. |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:343` | `DOUBLE_LOG_ALLOWED` is **empty and should stay that way**. It exists so a genuine exception is written down with its reason rather than the guard being loosened; an entry here means "these two rows are different events", never "this one is fine". |
| `tests/test_logkinds.py:516` | The default matters more than the call sites: one shared function defaulting to `VIA_WEBSITE` would silently turn every slash command's kind into a `web.` one. A private helper with a REQUIRED `via` is fine — it is always handed one. |
| `tests/api/conftest.py:405` | `one_web_row` is the per-route half of the same guard, and it is behavioural where the AST walk is structural: it asserts the write left exactly ONE `web.*` row, of the named kind, with `details.via == "website"`. Counting is the point — the old tests asserted both kinds were *present*, which is exactly what a double post looks like. |
| `black_bloc/logkinds.py:155` | Eight kinds left `ROUTINE` with this change (`event.cancel`, `honeypot.ban`, `mod.apply`, `mod.rule`, `modmail.close`, `poll.cancel`, `poll.end`, `tempvoice.forget`): each was only ever produced by a deleted `note()`, and `test_no_classification_entry_is_dead` refuses a table entry nothing emits. ⚠️ Legacy rows keep their kind and classify the same, with ONE exception — `honeypot.ban` ends in `.ban`, an `IMPORTANT_SUFFIXES` entry, so old `web.honeypot.ban` rows now read as important. That matches the new `honeypot.banned`, so it was left. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs:MOD_KIND_DONE` | The mock has to lie the same way the real API does: the punish helpers log what HAPPENED (`warned`, `timed_out`, `banned`), not what was asked for (`warn`, `timeout`, `ban`), so the mock maps the route name to the outcome word rather than logging the route name. `contract.json`'s `action_kinds` was updated in the same commit; `check.mjs` only checks emitted ⊆ listed, so a stale mock would have passed silently. |

# Requests — third pass: the review state, the embeds and the site link

> Keyed against `feat/requests-third-pass` at the commit named in the header
> line above. Owner, 2026-09-03: *"a standard appealing template … one of the
> discord info boxes"*, *"Do we need an acceptance pending so a staffer can check
> if something is done?"*. Design: [`requests-embeds-design.md`](requests-embeds-design.md).

| Key | Note |
|---|---|
| `black_bloc/requests.py:47` | ⚠️ **A LOOK is not a STATUS.** `LOOKS` has seven entries; `STATUSES` has seven too and they are **different sets**: `filed` and `sent_back` are looks with no state behind them, and `open` and `withdrawn` are states with no card. Everything downstream — the log kind, the colour, the fields, who is DMed, whether a card posts at all — reads the look, never the status. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:371` | `look_of` is the whole of that distinction in three lines: `in_progress` arrived at **from `review`** is `sent_back`. Storing a `sent_back` flag would have been a second home for a fact the `was:` already carries, and it would drift the first time somebody moved a row by hand. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:377` | `checked_move` grew two keyword-only text arguments rather than two new functions, because a move is judged in ONE place and the site, the slash commands and the tests all ask this. `TEXT_NEEDED` is keyed by LOOK (`review` needs `built`, `sent_back` needs `note`), which is why the required-text rule fires on a send-back and not on an ordinary pick-up — same target state, different look. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:154` | `DONE_NEEDS_A_CHECK` fires only from `OPEN_STATUSES`. From `declined` or `withdrawn` the generic "is where a request finishes" sentence is still right, and pointing somebody at `/request ready` there would be a lie. The refusal names both the slash path AND the site button, because the person reading it may be on either. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:228` | The colours are DATA (`EMBED_COLOURS`), and so are the titles, the field lists and the inline flags. Seven looks by four properties as literals inside one builder is how the sixth one quietly gets the fifth one's colour. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:612` | `moment` reads `created_at` for the filed card and `decided_at` for every other, so a card is stamped **when the move happened**. A row read back before `decided_at` is written (or a naive ISO string from an older row) falls back to now rather than raising — a card with a slightly wrong timestamp beats no card. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:637` | ⚠️ **`field_value` returning `""` is what leaves a field OFF the card.** Discord refuses an empty field value outright, so "How to test" on a review with none, "Assignee" on an unassigned row and "Due" with no date are absent rather than blank. Every value goes through `clamp(…, 1024)` here and nowhere else — §J measured the worst look at 2004 of Discord's 6000, entirely because of this line. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:688` | `site_view` answers `None` when there is no origin, and `post_line`/`dm` pass `view=None` straight through. A link button with a broken URL is worse than no button; `bot.settings.origin` is always set in practice, so this is the belt to the braces. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:703` | `move_line` is the plain one-liner that REPLACED the sent message — it is now only ever written to the server log, in `post_line`'s two `log.warning` calls, so a card the guard skipped still says in the log what it would have said. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:844` | `set_status` builds its `UPDATE` from a dict because five columns now have per-move rules and "leave this one alone" was already being faked with `COALESCE`. **A column with no rule for this move is not in the statement at all** — which is how `ready_by` survives a hold-and-resume and how `decided_by` survives a withdrawal. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:577` | `may_accept` answers True when nothing is recorded in `ready_by`. A row moved to `review` by the landing one-off, or by a `/status` write before this shipped, must not become unacceptable by anybody. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:348` | ⚠️ **`kind_via(f"request.{look}", via)` — LOOK, not status.** This is the line that makes `request.sent_back` exist at all; the row's status is `in_progress`. `tests/test_logkinds.py:KNOWN_DYNAMIC` is keyed on the source of that expression, so renaming the variable breaks the build loudly rather than silently dropping six kinds out of the classification check. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:172` | `person_told` is the ONE place that decides who gets a DM, and it is the reason `tell_requester` was renamed: on `sent_back` the person told is the staffer in `ready_by`, not the requester. Nobody is DMed on `review` — it is staff-facing and the channel card is its notice. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:193` | The `request_dm_on_decision` gate applies to `DM_LOOKS` only, so the send-back DM to `ready_by` is NOT gated by it. That key is documented as the **requester's** switch; widening it to staff notices would give one key two meanings and there would be no way to want one without the other. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:208` | `post_line` keeps its name and its `line` argument even though the line is never sent — the embed is the message and `content` is `None`. ⚠️ **The guard check is unmoved and unchanged**: TEST_MODE still refuses every channel but the test one and logs `request.notify_skipped_test_mode`, and a mutation that removes the check turns `test_the_review_card_is_skipped_and_logged_while_test_mode_holds_the_channel` red. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:298` | `apply_decision` passes `ready_by` and `sent_back_reason` on EVERY call and lets `set_status` decide whether this move writes them — the alternative, each caller working out which columns its move touches, is the same rule in five places. The `request_review_by_other` check lives here and not in `accept`, so `POST /{id}/status {"status":"done"}` cannot walk around it. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:395` | `send_back` is the only one of the three wrappers with a guard of its own: `accept` and `mark_ready` are refused by `TRANSITIONS` when the row is in the wrong state, but `review` → `in_progress` is legal from `open` too, so without this a `/request sendback` on an untouched request would quietly pick it up. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:883` | `ReadyModal` prefills from the row, so a request sent back and marked ready again does not need retyping. `built` is `required=True` at the Discord level AND refused in words by `checked_move` — the client-side one is a courtesy, the server-side one is the rule. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/community/requests.py:774` | `/request ready` is two interactions: the command opens the modal, the modal does the move. ⚠️ A modal can only be the FIRST response, so `_wanted_id` must not `defer()` — `require_staff` answers without deferring, which is why it can be called before `send_modal`. |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:499` | The three routes' whole job is `via=VIA_WEBSITE` and **no `note()`** — checklist 34. `tests/api/conftest.py:one_web_row` asserts exactly one `web.*` row per write, which is the assertion the pre-fix tests were missing (they asserted presence, which is what a double post looks like). |
| `black_bloc/api/tools/requests.py:575` | `/status` takes `built` and `how_to_test` as plain fields through `set_fields`, so fixing a typo in how-to-test is a partial save that leaves one `web.request.updated` row and moves nothing. It ALSO forwards them to `apply_decision` when a status is present, so `{"status":"review","built":…}` is a legal, if unused, second path into review. |
| `black_bloc/storage/db.py:11` | Schema **26**: four nullable columns on `requests` (`built`, `how_to_test`, `ready_by`, `sent_back_reason`), added to the `CREATE TABLE` and to `ADDED_COLUMNS`. No backfill — a row that was `done` before this stays `done` with four nulls, and `requests.py:row_value` reads a missing column as nothing on an older file. The landing move of #1 and #2 into `review` is a one-off in the design doc, **not** a migration: `done` → `review` is not a staff move and must not become one. |
| `black_bloc/settings_store.py:861` | `enums` is a NEW registry type — "any of these words", where `enum` is "one of" and `channels`/`roles` are lists of ids. `coerce_value` returns the picked set **in `KEY_CHOICES` order**, so the stored value is stable no matter what order the checkboxes were ticked in and two identical settings never diff. |
| `black_bloc/cogs/core.py:25` | ⚠️ `VALUE_KEYS` had to learn `enums` or `request_channel_moves` would have been a **dashboard-only** key — exactly half of checklist 33, and the half that is invisible until somebody tries `/settings set-value` and gets no autocomplete. `test_the_card_moves_key_is_reachable_from_slash_settings_as_well_as_the_dashboard` is the guard. |
| `site/public/assets/ui.js:928` | The `enums` control is a checkbox per choice, not a segment: a segment says "one of these", and the answer here is a SET. `read` walks the DOM rather than a captured array, so the value saved is what is actually ticked. |
| `black_bloc/requests.py:291` | `REQUEST_ANCHOR` takes its page from `logkinds.FEATURE_PAGES["request"]` — **`requests.html`, with the extension.** The design said `{origin}/requests#r-N` and the build shipped that; the site is a `StaticFiles(html=True)` mount (`api/assets.py`), which resolves `/requests` to a file called `requests` or `requests/index.html` and nothing else — live it answered `{"detail":"Not Found"}` (measured 2026-09-03 06:19, before the merge deployed). One home for the page name, so the log-embed links and the card button cannot drift apart. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:238` | ⚠️ **`anchored()` is what makes every Discord card's link button work.** Each card carries `id="r-{id}"`, and `{origin}/requests.html#r-{id}` is built in `black_bloc/requests.py:request_url`. The two halves are in different languages and nothing type-checks between them — `tests/test_requests.py::test_every_card_carries_one_link_button_to_the_request_on_the_site` pins the URL shape, and this is the other end of it. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:flashLinked` | ⚠️ **TWO things break a deep link into a shut section, and neither raises anything.** (1) A card inside a shut section or foldout — Done and Declined both are — sits in a `.card` with `overflow: hidden` and a **clientHeight of 32**, so `scrollIntoView` does nothing at all. (2) Opening the `<details>` is not enough on its own: the scroll must wait a **frame** for layout to settle, or it measures the collapsed height and stays put. Opening and scrolling in the same tick left the reader at the top of the page with nothing in the console. Measured against the mock: with the section open and one frame elapsed, `.content` (the real scroller — the body never scrolls) goes 0 → 3019 and the card lands mid-viewport. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:cardFor` | The pinned card is drawn as whatever the row actually IS. Drawing every one as a review card would put Accept and Send back on an open request, and the API would then refuse the click — the page's own rule is that a control which would be refused is never drawn. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:1202` | The off-page case: staff fetch `/api/requests/N`, a member scans their own `/mine`, and the result is PINNED above the sections with Back to all rather than paging the reader around. ⚠️ A 404 or a 403 here is "that number is not one you can read", **not** an outage — the two get different sentences, because the fixes are different. `pinned` is set before the fetch so a refresh mid-flight cannot pin twice. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:675` | The review card filters `done` and `in_progress` out of `row.moves` and draws Accept and Send back as its own buttons — those two moves need a dialog and a distinct label, which a generic move button cannot carry. `MOVES` lost its `done` entry entirely, so no card anywhere can draw a Done button. |
| `site/public/assets/page-requests.js:614` | `writtenRow` is a partial `/status` save, not a move: the owner asked that a typo in "how to test" not need a state change to fix. It is on the review card and on the done card, which is why `shutCard` builds a `notice()` only when the row is `done`. |
| `site/mock/server.mjs:askDecide` | The mock enforces the SAME three refusals the API does (no `built`, no send-back note, the second-pair-of-eyes rule) because `check.mjs` only checks that emitted kinds are a subset of the listed ones — a mock that accepted anything would pass while the real API refused. ⚠️ Its `/accept` and `/sendback` read the row AFTER the move; the pre-existing `/hold`, `/decline` and `/status` entries do not, and answer with the state the row was in. |
| `site/mock/check.mjs:IDS` | `review_request_id` (11) is a row the SEED already has ready to check, so `/accept` and `/sendback` reach it without walking the machine first — every contract entry runs against a fresh seed. `progress_request_id` (12) is where `/ready` is legal from. |
| `site/public/assets/labels.js:160` | ⚠️ **This file did not parse between `7b1c592` and the fix on this branch**, so `LABELS` never loaded and **every dashboard page rendered blank**. The Phase 19 merge pasted the applications block after the object's closing brace and after `NAMESPACES`, leaving seven orphaned properties and a second `};`. `node --check site/public/assets/labels.js` is the whole test, and it is worth running after any merge that touches this file — nothing else in the suite reads it. |

> ⚠️ **Re-keyed again 2026-09-03 at the wave-0 merge (`1861923`)** — seven rows whose code moved to
> `black_bloc/panels.py` now carry that path with a "was … until wave 0" note, and the cog keys

> panel's own-request list staff-only: every key in THIS section was shifted by anchor — the
> `requests.py` ones by **+1** (`PANEL_OWN_LIST_KEY` above them) or **+5** (`withdraw_request`,
> below `panel_shows_own_list` too), and the `cogs/community/requests.py` ones by **+1** above
> `build_panel` and **+2** below it (one import line, one `if`). `settings_store.py` +5;
> `api/tools/requests.py` unmoved. Two rows were ADDED (the gate at `:511`, the helper at
> `requests.py:512`); none was rewritten, because nothing they describe changed.
> Before that, keyed against `feat/requests-panel` at the commit this section was written in.
